Almanac

Orbits completed
The asteroid belt is drawn as 2,500 sample asteroids between 2.1 and 3.3 AU, with the Kirkwood gaps that Jupiter clears. The Kuiper belt (blue, 30 to 50 AU and beyond) shows its classical disc, the plutinos and the scattered disc. The Oort cloud, 2,000 to 100,000 AU out, has never been seen directly, so its shell is illustrative: zoom right out to find it.
Axes shows each body's spin axis, with the brighter end at its north pole, and each orbit's major axis, dotted from perihelion through the Sun to aphelion.
Comet tails point away from the Sun and grow as a comet nears it; their length is a sketch, not a measurement. Comets drift as the planets tug on them, so around each spacecraft visit the comet follows its orbit as it was then.
Tap or click any body, its label or its row here to centre on it and follow it. Tap the Sun to recentre. Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom.
Planet maps: Solar System Scope, CC BY 4.0. Stars: Hipparcos via d3-celestial. Milky Way: an impression of the band built from its galactic coordinates, not a photograph. Nearby stars: RECONS and Gaia distances via Wikipedia. Spacecraft: NASA JPL Horizons; the dashed paths beyond (Voyagers, Pioneers and New Horizons to 2100, Parker to 2030) are predicted from the last known position and velocity, coasting under the Sun’s gravity. Giotto, Vega 1 and 2, Suisei, Sakigake and ICE are not in Horizons, so their paths (dashed) are rebuilt as coasting arcs between their real launch, flyby and encounter dates. Comets: JPL Small-Body Database and Horizons. ISS: NORAD elements, SGP4 via satellite.js.
